# Euclid's GCD Remainder Identity

## The identity to remember

$$
\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(b,a\bmod b)
$$

**Every symbol explained:** gcd is greatest common divisor; a,b are nonnegative integers, b>0; mod computes the remainder.

**Substitute actual numbers:** gcd(48,18)=gcd(18,12)=gcd(12,6)=gcd(6,0)=6.

## Why it is true

Any common divisor of a and b divides a−qb, the remainder, and any divisor of b and the remainder divides a=qb+r. Thus both pairs have identical common divisors.

## Algorithm or puzzle application

Use when finding a largest equal group size or simplifying ratios, or in modular calculations.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

The recurrence needs b>0; terminate with gcd(a,0)=a. gcd(0,0) has convention-dependent treatment.

## Your turn

Compute gcd(252,105) using remainders.

**Memory rule:** Prove the factor or remainder relationship instead of treating the identity as a magic shortcut.
